points_of_interest.name: Saint-Julien-du-Sault Church
points_of_interest.description: Saint-Pierre Church, former collegiate church that possesses magnificent stained glass windows from the 13th century, and a Renaissance organ, dated 1568. Around the edifice, the typical streets, beautiful buildings like the chapter house and the Archbishop's house give the village a lot of charm.

points_of_interest.name: Saint-Julien-du-Sault Chapelle de Vauguillan
points_of_interest.description: In the high part of the village rises the Chapel Saint-Julien de Vauguillain, remnant of Castle Vauguillain, protected by fortifications. Chapel and ramparts form a beautiful photogenic ensemble, and the location offers a beautiful view of the valley, and the surrounding green landscape.

museum of cultural heritage (musée du patrimoine culturel) of Saint-Julien-du-Sault. 

Housed in a half-timbered house from the 16th century, this museum is dedicated to historical trades and life of the past, and has a rich collection of ancient objects and instruments.

points_of_interest.description:
Jovinien - Cote Saint Jacques
Chardonnay/Pinot gris/Pinot noir

The first mention of vines in Joigny in 1082. 

The town was built between the forest, the vineyards and the Yonne river:  wood for houses and barrels, vineyards for trade and water for the river transport of wood and wine. 

- The hillsides sheltered from the north wind 
 -face south/southeast,  - on soft limestone soil covered with clay 
- microclimate due to the river.

the cultivation of vines contributed to the town's economic development. 
In 1776, there were 574 hectares of vines. After its destruction by phylloxera at the end of the 19th century, the Pinot gris and Pinot noir grape varieties were replanted. 

Today, some forty hectares produce white wines from the Chardonnay grape and red wines from Pinot noir. The town is also famous for its Vin Gris, produced from the Pinot Gris grape.
